title: Shlomo Gave the Torah Handles
summary: Shlomo Hamelech instituted eruvin and netilas yadayim, and Hashem said "My son, be wise and gladden My heart." Then "Come, my beloved, let us go out to the field": Klal Yisrael early in the shuls and batei medrash. Shlomo's three thousand meshalim, how he gave the Torah "handles" so people could hold it, the tagin on every letter that hold mounds of halachos, and the Torah that stays with one who is cruel to himself like a raven to its young.
key_ideas: When two good things compete, a wise person weighs what each one brings.
Shlomo gave the Torah handles: meshalim, signs and fences that let people hold it.
Every crown on a letter holds mounds of halachos.
Torah stays with one who rises early, stays late, and sets aside the comforts of this world.
